<reason>Side B exposed the fatal tension in PRO's case: preventing buyer fraud (swap-and-return) requires physical custody chains, but the motion's scope includes everyday clothing where percentage commissions cannot cover flat logistics costs. PRO's proposed solutions (tiered fees, AI/photo screening) either shift costs to consumers or contradict their opening claim that photos cannot catch sophisticated fakes. CON maintained that platforms already tier appropriately and that the motion would destroy the unit economics of peer-to-peer resale.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 (B4.1-B4.5) dismantling A's economic alternatives (tiered fees, AI screening) as either cost-shifting or contradictory to A's opening, combined with B's Closing highlighting A's concession that physical verification is the only mechanism to prevent swap scams.</best_rebuttal>
